notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level and never a hardware run). The package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null, so the loader refuses the R2 hardware backend until a human signs it. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the driver is a decorated direct Driver (ElveflowOB1), not the card's PythonObjectDriver helper, because the OB1 needs an explicit e-stop and safe-state action and a per-channel state. The card lists MUXelve and OB1elve as entry symbols; this package implements OB1elve only, so the 1-to-12 MUX valve distributor is NOT COVERED. Also NOT COVERED: sensor configuration (OB1elve.addSensor), PID setup and tuning (remoteAddPID, remoteChangePID, remoteSetTarget), and pressure calibration (performCallibration); flow reads require a sensor already configured, as in readme.md:30-32. Pressure writes are Limit.operator_required because the range follows the installed regulator type (pycrofluidics/elveob.py:543-553) and no text states the range of the configured unit; site-limits.example.json is an example overlay (0 to 200 mbar), not a statement about any unit, and every pressure write is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the operator supplies site-limits.json. The e-stop and x-cap.wetenschaap.stop_remote.v1 stop the remote loop and command all four pressure channels to 0 mbar. The fake is an in-memory stand-in, not a recording; its pressure and flow values are placeholders and never move by themselves. native.py (the hardware factory) was never imported or run. gate.digest is the digest line the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
